Not to the enemy: nobody would dream of saying that. {ag_He} has simply stopped answering your letters, and {ag_his} tax receipts have stopped, and in {auh_region} they have started to date things from the year that {ag_he} arrived. It is all being done very politely. Every one of your own generals has now seen how it is done, and you can tell they are all thinking very carefully.

choices.text: Let it be known that anyone can have that deal, if they ask first

effects.log: One of them does ask. It is the most frightening conversation of your life, and it goes well.

choices.text: March on {ag_him} next year, whatever else it costs

effects.log: Your officers nod. They will march. You see them looking at the rest of the map, working out what it costs.

events.text: {auh_gen} has died at the front. It was not in the battle. {ag_He} had been coughing for a year and telling nobody. They have sent you {ag_his} seal, and the last set of accounts, which are correct, and a short list of officers who should be promoted, in order, and why. The final line is about the mules. You have read a great many of these. You sit for a long time with this one before you send for anybody.

choices.text: Bring {ag_him} home, on your own carriage

effects.log: It takes three months. The whole road turns out. They are not there for you, and you find that you do not mind.

choices.text: Bury {ag_him} where {ag_he} fell, and promote the list

effects.log: You promote the list, in order, as written. You have never in your life done anything that {ag_he} would have liked better.

events.text: A very young officer has brought you the news, and he is not doing it well. {auh_gen} went forward to see it in person, as {ag_he} always did. It was a stray arrow from nobody in particular, a long way from anything, on a nice day. {ag_He} said something about it being annoying, and that was all. The young officer has been holding {ag_his} hat all this time. He does not seem to know that he has it.

choices.text: Take the hat, and sit him down

effects.log: You sit with him for a while. There is a great deal to do, and you do not do any of it until after he has stopped shaking.

choices.text: Ask who has the command now

effects.log: It is the right question, and he answers it. He stands up very straight. You keep the hat.

events.text: The enemy has returned the body of {auh_gen}, with every honour. There are eight of their officers walking beside it, in white, and their own commander has written you a letter in a very fine hand. They have never met anyone like {ag_him}, it says. They also enclose a bill for the coffin. It is, they feel, what {ag_he} would have wanted, and you find that you agree.

choices.text: Pay it, double, and send it back with your own honour guard

effects.log: It is the only laugh you have had this year, and you cannot tell anyone why. {ag_He} would have checked the addition.

choices.text: Have the eight officers shown every courtesy, and a good dinner

effects.log: You sit down with them. Nobody talks about the war. You learn some things about {ag_him} you had never known.

events.text: There is an old soldier at your gate who will not give his name. He has walked from the other front to tell you how {auh_gen} died, and he says it was a good death, and then he stops. You wait. He tells you it was not, in fact, a good death. It took four days. {ag_He} spent most of it asking whether you had got the grain through. He wanted you to know, he says, because nobody else was going to tell you that.

choices.text: Thank him, and give him a house

effects.log: He will not take the house. He takes a meal, and a pair of boots, and he goes back the way he came.

choices.text: Tell him that the grain got through

effects.log: It did not, as it happens. He looks at you for quite a while. "Yes," he says. "That is what I told {ag_him}."

events.text: You have been gone for most of three years, and the capital has discovered that it can run without you. It is doing it rather well. A dispatch has reached the front from {auh_home}'s Grand Secretary, asking your approval on a number of matters, and the dates on them show that they were already settled. It is all quite respectful. There is, you notice, a new seal on the documents, a small one, in a very clean hand.

choices.text: Ride back for a month, unannounced

effects.log: It costs the campaign a month. You walk through the Hall of Supreme Harmony in travelling clothes, and the seal is gone by evening.

choices.text: Approve them all. You have a war to win

effects.log: You sign. The capital sends its thanks. It seems to you that there are somewhat fewer of them each time.

events.text: The Censors have sent a memorial to you at the front, signed by forty of them, and the Grand Censor has had the courage to bring it himself. There are famine reports from Henan. It says that the war tax has taken the seed grain, and the memorial is very beautifully written, and it says that Heaven has noticed. He is seventy-nine, he has come a very long way, and nobody has asked him to sit.

choices.text: Remit the tax in Henan, and ask him to sit

effects.log: It costs you two regiments' pay. He sits. He looks at you for a long while, and he says that Heaven may notice that, too.

choices.text: Thank him, and send him home by the slow road

effects.log: He goes. Forty Censors have a great deal to write down about it, and they are very careful about the dates.

events.text: Your second cousin has written to say that the house is perfectly well, and the treasury is perfectly safe, and that as you are likely to be away for a long time, some of the elders feel it would be a kindness to spare you the burden of the small matters. A list of the small matters is enclosed. It includes the seal, the marriages of the next generation, and the deed to the ancestral hall.

choices.text: Reply with a new will, copied to every branch

effects.log: It is a very short will. The small matters are returned to you by the next post, with apologies.

choices.text: Leave it for now. You have an empire to take

effects.log: They are very grateful. Your own name comes up less and less in the letters from home.

events.text: The house has lost two sons on your fronts this year, and they were both from the same branch. Their mother has come all the way to your camp, and she has brought the family tablet with her and set it down on your map table, right on top of the Salt Pasture. You have been sitting across from it for an hour. It is a very old tablet, and your own name is carved rather further down on it.

choices.text: Send her youngest home, with an honour, and go with her to the road

effects.log: Your officers have seen it. You have kept a son alive, and she takes the tablet away, and you can look at your map again.

choices.text: Have the tablet carried with the army

effects.log: She lets you take it. She goes home by herself. You have told everyone what the house is for now.

events.text: Elder Baek has written from the stores. There is a feud, he says, with the next valley. It has been going for a hundred and sixty years and it had been going very nicely. But now, with all your best people gone to the end of the earth, the next valley has noticed. They have moved a boundary stone by about a foot. It is the sort of thing a clan head would normally see to. He only wanted it written down.

choices.text: Send the best captain you have, for one season

effects.log: A company of your best goes home to deal with a stone. The next valley puts it back, very quickly, and sends some ducks.

choices.text: Let them have the foot of ground

effects.log: They take it. Next year, it is two feet. Elder Baek has written that down too.

events.text: A clan's children have to be taught by someone. You have just had a letter from a small girl in the third branch, who has been told that she will be clan head one day, if everyone else dies. She wishes to know how the war is going, and if there is anyone left who can show her the second form properly, as the old man who has been teaching her does it wrong.

choices.text: Send her a veteran, and a real answer

effects.log: It costs you a good sergeant. He writes that he has never been so frightened in his life, and that she has got it right.

choices.text: Send her a sword, and tell her to keep trying

effects.log: It is a very good sword. She writes back that it is too long, and that you did not answer the question.

events.text: There are almost no disciples in the outer court these days. The Discipline Hall has written to say that it has been sweeping the steps itself. The forms are going out of true: there is nobody left between the very old and the very young to show how a thing is done. A boy of nine has corrected an elder, and was right. The Elder has written to you about it, and you can tell that he is not sure what to ask you for.

choices.text: Send a hundred seniors home to teach

effects.log: It is a real gap in your line. Next year the steps are swept by the people who should be sweeping them.

choices.text: Tell them to do what they can

effects.log: They do what they can. The sect will have a hole in it, one generation deep, for the next hundred years.

events.text: A rival sect has sent very polite condolences on the long march, and has offered to send a respected Teacher up the mountain, in the circumstances. The Teacher has arrived, and has been very well received, and has been given the good guest quarters. The Sect Elder writes to say that he can see no way to refuse, under the rules, and that the Teacher is quite good. That, he adds, is what worries him.

choices.text: Write the Teacher a personal invitation to your front

effects.log: It is an invitation that cannot be refused either. They are very good. You have them teaching your scouts within the month.

choices.text: Let it pass. It is only teaching

effects.log: It is only teaching. In ten years your own disciples will be doing the forms just slightly in another way.

events.text: Three of the Elders you left behind in the Hundred Thousand Mountains have decided that the Hall of Black Pillars needs a new roof, which will have to be paid for out of your own treasury. You have been told that the work involves moving a large number of very loyal guards to the lower gate. In the Cult this is more or less how one says good morning. They would be most disappointed if you did not notice.

choices.text: Send them a very small box, with your compliments

effects.log: It is empty, as it happens. They spend a whole season working out what that means. The roof is left as it is.

choices.text: Let them play. You will settle it when you return

effects.log: They are very pleased. It is a splendid roof. You are going to have some trouble getting back under it.

events.text: Your own Cult's rule has always been that strength is law. It has now occurred to the demonic sects outside it that you are a very long way away, and it has occurred to the orthodox ones that the Mountains are empty. You have a letter from a Hall Master you left there. It is one line, and rather shaky. It reads: "They have both turned up at once, and they have noticed each other. What would you like done?"

choices.text: Tell the demons about the Orthodox, and the Orthodox about the demons

effects.log: You spend a very pleasant evening writing the two letters. They are all too busy with one another for some years.

choices.text: Tell the Hall Master to hold, and pray

effects.log: The Hall Master holds. He does not pray, he is a demonic cultivator. A good part of the lower Mountains is on fire now.

events.text: The Alliance has held an Assembly without you. It was entirely in order. It was called to discuss whether the Leader should be asked to report on the progress of the war, in person, in view of the expense. Wudang moved it, and the Namgung seconded it, and Shaolin abstained, in a very loud voice. Old Master Gwak writes that you still have your majority, for a year or perhaps two, and that it is getting smaller.

choices.text: Send every member sect a share of the spoils, publicly

effects.log: It is a very large share. Your treasurers are in tears. The next Assembly votes you a very warm letter of thanks.

choices.text: Tell them they may report to you, when you are done

effects.log: They read it out at the Assembly. It is much admired for its style. Nobody voted for you on the strength of your style.

events.text: A young master of the Hua has just been killed at the Alliance's gate, in a duel, with a demonic sect, over nothing, and there is nobody left at home with the standing to stop it going any further. It would normally have been settled by the Leader in an afternoon. Both sides are asking you to judge from the far side of the world, and every day you take is costing lives that you have never heard of.

choices.text: Judge it by letter, and send a master with your seal to see it done

effects.log: You send your best. It takes months, and it holds. They do not know what it costs you to have them gone from the front.

choices.text: Say that it can wait until you return

effects.log: It does not wait. There is quite a small war going on at home now, and it is all in your name.

events.text: An inspector from the capital has turned up in your camp with an extremely good memory. {auh_home} has every confidence in you, he explains. He would only like to count the soldiers. He is quite pleasant, and he has brought his own lunch. It has been explained to you by people who have been in the army for a long time that nobody comes all this way to count anything.

choices.text: Open everything to him, and let him count

effects.log: It takes a month. They are exactly the right number, and he goes back with that. You have made him look a little foolish, and it is a very long memory.

choices.text: Have him shown a very good time, in the wrong camp

effects.log: He writes down everything, and he thanks you for the fine dinners. It is all in his report, in order, with the dates.

events.text: They have stopped your pay. It is an oversight, at the very highest level, and it will surely be put right. It has been an oversight for eleven months now. You have also learned that a man has been named your deputy, and that he comes from a very good family. He will shortly be arriving with a very fine set of orders. It would seem that the throne has been reading about how far you have come.

choices.text: Make him welcome, and hand him the worst sector

effects.log: It is a very hard sector. He turns out to be brave, and not a fool. You will have to tell the Ministry that, and it does not please them.

choices.text: Pay the army from what you have taken, and keep it quiet

effects.log: The soldiers get their silver from your hand. They begin to forget where it was supposed to come from. So, in the capital, do they not.

events.text: A letter from {auh_kin}. It is not long. The plum tree at the gate has flowered. The roof wants mending. Someone has had a cold, and is over it. It has taken nine weeks to reach you, on the fastest horses in the world, across three provinces that belong to you, and it says nothing at all about any of those things, and you have read it about eleven times. You are told the courier is waiting for a reply.

choices.text: Write back, at length, about nothing

effects.log: You write about the weather and the food, and a dog you have met. It is the best thing that you have done all year.

choices.text: Send gold for the roof

effects.log: They get the roof mended. The next letter is shorter, and it thanks you for the gold.

events.text: {auh_kin} has come to the front. Nobody told you. There has been a very long journey, on bad roads, and now there is a person you know standing in the door of your tent, looking at the maps, and looking at you. You have got much older, they observe. They would like to know what it is all for, and when it stops. You have a great many good answers to that. You gave them to the ministers only this morning.

choices.text: Give up the morning, and walk with them on the wall

effects.log: You do not give any of the answers. They stay for a week, and they tell you who has died, and what has been planted.

choices.text: Have them shown to the good quarters, and go back to the maps

effects.log: They are very comfortable. They go home at the end of the month. You keep meaning to find an evening.

events.text: Your household has sent you a painting, by someone quite good, of the way everybody looks now. {auh_kin} is in it, near the middle, and you stand looking at it for a while before you realise that the very tall person beside them is a child you left at about the height of a table. You have had a good deal of practice at reading a large country from a small map. It is rather harder to do with this.

choices.text: Have it hung in the tent, where the staff can see

effects.log: They do not say anything. Several of them get out their own. It is a strange sort of evening, and nobody works.

choices.text: Roll it up carefully, for later

effects.log: You keep it in the map case, where it will be safe. It is there for years. It is very well preserved.

events.text: You are told that {auh_kin} has been ill, and that it is over now, and that you were not told at the time because there was a campaign on and it would not have helped. It would not have helped. There was absolutely nothing you could have done from where you were. You spend the rest of the day signing things, very neatly. Your secretary has twice now brought you the same paper, and you have twice signed it.

choices.text: Give a standing order: you are to be told, always

effects.log: Your staff are very shaken. It means that you will now hear of every cough at home, in the middle of every battle. You do.

choices.text: Say nothing about it, and go on

effects.log: You go on. It is what they wanted you to do, as it happens, and they have told you so, and you can see that they meant it.

events.text: A small package has come from home. It holds one of your old practice shoes, a wooden top, a sprig of something dry, and a piece of paper in the handwriting of {auh_kin}, with a single line. "We did not know if you would want them." There is an army of a hundred thousand people outside this tent, who all think that you know what you want. You move the map a bit, and you put the top on the table, and you try it.

choices.text: Send them your old seal, as a toy

effects.log: It is a very dangerous thing to send a child, and it is the only joke that you have made this year. They write back about it.

choices.text: Put them away, and pick up the next dispatch

effects.log: It is from the left wing. It is very urgent. They all are.

events.text: {auh_region} has risen. On the same night, every one of your wells was found to be full of dead sheep, and your tax clerks were found all together, tied up, unhurt, on a very high hill with a very good view, with their ledgers beside them. The clans are nowhere. There is a new name going round that nobody will say in front of you, and a very young chief who has the look of someone you once let go.

choices.text: Ride them down, again, and salt the pasture

effects.log: It takes a whole season. You hold the province. It holds nothing but you.

choices.text: Go to the young chief, with few riders

ok.log: You sit up all night, and it is very cold. You leave with a treaty and with a good deal less tax. It lasts.

fail.log: You are lucky to get out of it, and the province goes with them.

choices.text: Let it go. Hold the rest

effects.log: You let it go. Your officers do not look at you. The clans have a very good feast, and they save you a place.

events.text: It is the second winter, and the grain carts have not reached {auh_region}, and your garrison has started to take what it wants. It has not gone well. The old women of the Salt Pasture have all stopped counting lambs for you. They have come out and sat around your last fort, with their spindles, and they are saying nothing and looking at the gate, and your commander has written to you to ask what he is to do.

choices.text: Hang him, and send the grain at any cost

effects.log: It costs two campaigns' worth. The spindles go home, one at a time. They may have been counting something else.

choices.text: Go and sit with them

ok.log: After three days someone gives you a spindle. You are very bad at it. The forts stop burning.

fail.log: You sit there for three days. They go on not looking at you. Then the fort burns, with you standing in front of it.

choices.text: Pull the garrison out while you can

effects.log: They march out through the spindles, at a very slow walk, and nobody says a word. It is the longest mile of the war.

events.text: The river has risen in {auh_region}, and so has everyone on it. A very old abbot sat down on a pile of wood and sent you a polite letter about the water law, and he has now gone up, in full view of a very large crowd, and the Delta has come out behind his ashes with rice flails, barge poles, and a really astonishing number of bees. Your magistrates have barricaded themselves in the granary, and are writing to you.

choices.text: Send the army. All of it

effects.log: The barges burn for a month. You keep the Delta. The ashes are carried away down all Nine Rivers, in very small boxes.

choices.text: Repeal the water law in the abbot's name

ok.log: They go home by the thousand. No one thanks you. They go back to their terraces and start paying the taxes they were paying before.

fail.log: Too late. A repeal only tells them that they were winning.

choices.text: Get your magistrates out, and let it have the Delta

effects.log: You do get them out. They all want to explain what happened, and you do not read it.

events.text: There is a rumour in {auh_region} that the old queen's child is alive, and that the child is living in a rice village, up past the cloud line, and that a white elephant has knelt to them. Your garrison has arrested eleven children and let ten go, and nobody can agree which one it still has. Every village on the terraces is growing a little less rice, and you have not quite been able to work out how.

choices.text: Burn the upper villages

effects.log: It works. There is no rice from the upper terraces, or anyone, and no more rumour.

choices.text: Have the child found, and treat with them

ok.log: They are about eleven. They are terribly serious. You make a treaty with a very small person and a very large elephant, and it holds.

fail.log: You find another one. And then you find another. In the end nobody is paying you any rice at all.

choices.text: Let the terraces go

effects.log: You let them go. It costs you the whole of the province, and it saves you a very great deal of rope.

events.text: Every lord in {auh_region} has, on the same morning, politely returned your seal. They have gone back to their castles. It seems that a lord you beat has now been beaten by someone else, in a duel, on a beach, somewhere you had no one watching, and under the rule of the Isles that means all of those who swore to you are now sworn to the young person who beat him. Nobody can see why you are upset.

choices.text: Go and fight the young person yourself

ok.log: It is quite short. They all send their seals back to you by the next tide, with a very nice poem, and it is as if nothing had happened.

fail.log: It is quite short. They bow to you, very respectfully. The province is theirs.

choices.text: Send the fleet, and end this custom for ever

effects.log: You burn four castles. There are no more duels on the beach. They are held somewhere else now, at night.

choices.text: Accept it, and recognise them

effects.log: You send a nice letter. They are delighted. They invite you for tea, if you would ever care to visit their islands.

events.text: The sailors of {auh_region} have stopped. No one has been rude to anyone. They have simply brought all the ships back into harbour, taken the sails off, and folded them, and gone home to mend things. Nothing can move between your islands, and your garrisons are starting to eat their boots. An old woman in a boat comes by every morning, smoking her pipe, to ask whether you have anything that you would like to say.

choices.text: Say it

ok.log: You say it from the end of a jetty, in the rain, in very bad dialect. It seems to have been the right thing. By morning there are sails.

fail.log: She takes the pipe out of her mouth and looks at it. "No," she says, and rows on. That is the last boat you see.

choices.text: Bring your own crews, and hang anyone who stops them

effects.log: Your own crews put a third of the fleet on the rocks in a month. The rest get through. So you still have the islands, in a manner of speaking.

choices.text: Take the garrisons off, in what floats

effects.log: You get most of them. You are very careful not to thank the old woman, and she tows the rest.

events.text: Every prayer wheel in {auh_region} has started to turn the other way. Your governor has written very calmly to say that it matters. It seems that nobody up there will now sell to you, or carry for you, or look at you, and that none of it is disrespect. The whole plateau is praying for you, by name, day and night. Your soldiers have started to desert.

choices.text: Have the wheels smashed

effects.log: It takes a year and there are a very great many of them. The people go on doing it with their hands.

choices.text: Climb up and ask the abbots what they are praying for

ok.log: They are praying for you to be happy. It is the most terrible thing you have ever heard. You come to terms. The wheels change direction, more or less.

fail.log: They show you to the door, the short one. You bend, and you come out, and it is not your province any more.

choices.text: Withdraw to the lower forts

effects.log: You go. Behind you on the road there is that very quiet sound, going on and on.

events.text: The caravan masters have raised the toll. That is all that has happened in {auh_region}. They have the charter you yourself gave them, and clause nine is really very well drafted. It has now become a little cheaper to send your army's grain by way of the moon. Dawa has come to explain this, with some apricots, and with a good deal of sympathy, and a very long face. He would be glad to discuss it.

choices.text: Sit down, and read clause nine

ok.log: It takes a week, and you find clause thirty. Dawa looks at it for a long time, and takes an apricot, and laughs till he cries. The toll comes down.

fail.log: It takes a week. You get a headache and a very good apricot. By then, the whole Oasis Road has made other arrangements.

choices.text: Hang Dawa and burn the charter

effects.log: You can do that. The Road goes dark from end to end. It is a very long time before you can buy so much as a rug.

choices.text: Give up the road, and keep your dignity

effects.log: You give it up. Dawa is really very nice about it. There are still apricots from time to time.

events.text: They have shown you the war room, and you had not understood that it was this big. {auh_held} regions are held in the name you have just been given. You are told, by people who do not meet your eye, that all of them were expecting someone a good deal older. A very old secretary brings you the box of dispatches for today, and sets it down. "There will be another tomorrow," he says, with some sympathy.

choices.text: Read them, all of them, tonight

effects.log: It takes until dawn. At the end of it you know very little, and you have a great many people who now think you might be worth following.

choices.text: Ask him which of them matters

effects.log: He looks at you properly, for the first time. "Ah," he says. He starts to take out the ones that do not.

events.text: The conquered provinces have all sent to you, at the funeral, by envoys who are extremely correct. They grieve. Are you bound, they ask, by what was promised? It is the first thing that anyone has asked you since you sat down here, and all of your generals are now very carefully looking at the floor. There are at least four people in this room who could have you killed by the end of the week.

choices.text: "Every word." Whatever it was

effects.log: They bow. You find out later what it was, and it is very expensive. You keep it. The four people notice that.

choices.text: "I will read what was promised, and then I will tell you."

effects.log: That takes them by surprise, and your generals too. It is, at any rate, not what the last one would have said.

events.text: You have inherited a very large war, and a general, who has come to pay their respects, and stays standing. They have served your parent for thirty years. They look you up and down. "Do you want it?" they ask. Nobody has ever said this to you. It is a real question, and you can tell by the way the staff have all stopped breathing that it is the only one that you are ever going to be asked.

choices.text: "Yes."

effects.log: They wait a moment longer. Then they go down on one knee, slowly, because of the left one, and the rest of the room comes down behind them.

choices.text: "No. But nobody else in this room should have it."

effects.log: They begin to laugh, and it takes them some time. "That is what your parent said," they tell you. "Get up."

events.text: There is nothing left on the map. Your clerks have been redrawing it for a month, and now all four corners are in the same ink. Every envoy in the Hall of Supreme Harmony has become a governor. Nobody knows how the ceremony ought to go, so you have had to make it up. The Grand Secretary reads out the words "All Under Heaven", and that is all. You look up. It is a clear, bright, empty day, and it has gone very quiet.

choices.text: Stand there until the sun goes down

effects.log: You stand. Nobody dares to move. At dusk, one star comes out, in the wrong place.

choices.text: Ask what is for dinner

effects.log: It is the only laugh in the hall, and it goes on too long. Above you, one star has come out in the middle of the afternoon.

events.text: The last envoy has laid the last seal at the foot of the steps. You had five crowns brought in, so that you could see them, and you have found that you do not know what to do about them. You might wear one. You could have them melted down. The eunuchs have started to back out of the room, and none of them has looked up at the roof, though there is a very odd light coming through it.

choices.text: Have them melted into one plain thing

effects.log: It is a heavy, ugly thing, and nobody will ever be comfortable under it. It will do. The light through the roof does not go away.

choices.text: Leave them there, and go out to see the sky

effects.log: You go out on the terrace. The sky is just as it was. There is something very like attention in it.

events.text: Your house holds all of it. There are cousins of yours governing the Khaganate and the Nine Rivers, and they are all writing to you about their in-laws. {auh_home} has sent the Dragon Seal to you in a plain box, with a short note, and asks only to be allowed to keep the name and the gardens. You go down to the ancestral hall, and the tablets have all fallen over, every one, face up.

choices.text: Go out and look up

effects.log: You go out. It is only the sky. It has never looked back at you before.

choices.text: Finish what is in front of you first

effects.log: You finish it, and you sign it. You do not look up for the rest of the day. You can feel it just the same.

events.text: A clerk has finished the family register, and it now runs to every province under the sky. He has had to invent a new sort of binding. He brings it to you for the seal. {auh_home} still sits on the throne in the capital, because you have let them. There is nobody left to marry, you notice, who is not already a relation. The whole house is asleep. There is a person standing in the courtyard looking up, and it is you.

choices.text: Wait for it, then

effects.log: You pour a second cup, and set it out for whoever is coming.

choices.text: Have the watch doubled

effects.log: You have it doubled. They are very good soldiers, and they are all looking in the wrong direction, and you know it.

events.text: It started with a boundary stone. You find you are thinking of that, this morning, with all five empires kneeling in a field outside your clan compound, because there was nowhere else to put them. {auh_home} has come in person, to hand you a seal, and has been given a good lunch by Elder Baek. You go up to the old watchtower to have a look, and the sky has an odd, listening look to it.

choices.text: Go out and look up

effects.log: You go out. It is only the sky. It has never looked back at you before.

choices.text: Finish what is in front of you first

effects.log: You finish it, and you sign it. You do not look up for the rest of the day. You can feel it just the same.

events.text: Your crest flies over every city on the map. It is the same crest. It still has that small stain in the corner, from a very bad dinner your great-grandfather once had. Every court there is has had to learn to draw it. {auh_home} has sent to ask how you would like to be addressed, and the whole clan has been laughing about it for a week. You are the only one who has noticed that the birds have all stopped.

choices.text: Wait for it, then

effects.log: You pour a second cup, and set it out for whoever is coming.

choices.text: Have the watch doubled

effects.log: You have it doubled. They are very good soldiers, and they are all looking in the wrong direction, and you know it.

events.text: There is no one left to fight. The disciples have come back up the mountain, all that are coming, and they have brought their empires with them. {auh_home} has sent you the Dragon Seal by an old monk. You set it on the lectern, and you open at the first page, the one about breath. Everyone is looking at you. It is a fine night, and it has begun, very softly, to thunder without any clouds.

choices.text: Go out and look up

effects.log: You go out. It is only the sky. It has never looked back at you before.

choices.text: Finish what is in front of you first

effects.log: You finish it, and you sign it. You do not look up for the rest of the day. You can feel it just the same.

events.text: The whole world is one sect, a very junior disciple points out, with some surprise. Under the rules, she says, that makes everyone a fellow student, and so nobody can properly fight anyone without the permission of the Discipline Hall. She seems quite serious. You begin to laugh, and then you see that the incense smoke is going straight up, and has stopped there.

choices.text: Wait for it, then

effects.log: You pour a second cup, and set it out for whoever is coming.

choices.text: Have the watch doubled

effects.log: You have it doubled. They are very good soldiers, and they are all looking in the wrong direction, and you know it.

events.text: It is all yours. Six hundred years of being the end of the world in other people's stories, and you have gone and made it come true, and everyone is paying their taxes. The old Grand Elder has been carried up to see it. He looks out over the whole of it from the top of the Hall of Black Pillars. "Well," says the Elder at last. "Now they will have to send somebody." He does not sound as if he means any human being.

choices.text: Go out and look up

effects.log: You go out. It is only the sky. It has never looked back at you before.

choices.text: Finish what is in front of you first

effects.log: You finish it, and you sign it. You do not look up for the rest of the day. You can feel it just the same.

events.text: There is no one who is not afraid of you, and you had wondered what that would be like. Every sect has opened its gate, and all of the orthodox masters have sent their keys. {auh_home} has sent theirs in a jewelled case. The Cult has been holding a feast for nine days. On the tenth, every black banner in the Hundred Thousand Mountains stops moving, all at once, in a good wind, and it is not your doing.

choices.text: Wait for it, then

effects.log: You pour a second cup, and set it out for whoever is coming.

choices.text: Have the watch doubled

effects.log: You have it doubled. They are very good soldiers, and they are all looking in the wrong direction, and you know it.

events.text: It is the last Spring Assembly there will ever need to be. All the world's seals are lying on one table. Wudang has agreed with Shaolin. {auh_home} has sent the Dragon Seal to be laid with them, and has asked only to be let alone. Old Master Gwak is too old to stand now, and they have carried him out. He wants to know who is going to hold the door. He is looking straight up.

choices.text: Go out and look up

effects.log: You go out. It is only the sky. It has never looked back at you before.

choices.text: Finish what is in front of you first

effects.log: You finish it, and you sign it. You do not look up for the rest of the day. You can feel it just the same.

events.text: You have the paper, with every seal on it. It says that there is one house, and that you keep its door. There is nobody on the far side of the door. You go over this several times. {auh_home} has written to congratulate you, in their own hand, and to say that they are looking forward to their retirement. It is very late, and you are out on the steps with a cup, when the stars begin, very slightly, to lean.

choices.text: Wait for it, then

effects.log: You pour a second cup, and set it out for whoever is coming.

choices.text: Have the watch doubled

effects.log: You have it doubled. They are very good soldiers, and they are all looking in the wrong direction, and you know it.

events.text: There are no more frontiers. It is what you promised them. The cook from the Liaodong camp, who is a colonel by now, has made you a very bad supper. {auh_home} has sent you a yellow cloak, by a very nervous eunuch, and asks you what your intentions are. You have a look at it. It is a very nice cloak. Someone has just stopped singing, a long way away, and now no one is singing.

choices.text: Go out and look up

effects.log: You go out. It is only the sky. It has never looked back at you before.

choices.text: Finish what is in front of you first

effects.log: You finish it, and you sign it. You do not look up for the rest of the day. You can feel it just the same.

events.text: You have brought them to the end of the world, and they are standing on it. Your warrant has run out. It says "until the enemies of the throne are subdued", and you have read it again, and there are none. {auh_home} has written to say so, very gratefully. There are two million soldiers out there who have no idea what to do with themselves, and they are all looking at you. Then, rank upon rank, they look up.

choices.text: Wait for it, then

effects.log: You pour a second cup, and set it out for whoever is coming.

choices.text: Have the watch doubled

effects.log: You have it doubled. They are very good soldiers, and they are all looking in the wrong direction, and you know it.

events.text: There is a small grey person on your steps, with a ledger, who got past every guard by not being noticed. They are Ok-Seo, a Recorder of the Jade Court above the clouds, and they keep the Mandate Rolls. Your name is on the last page, and nobody is supposed to fill the last page. They have come to say, without heat, that the Court will take it from here. You may lay it all down and be remembered kindly, or not.

choices.text: Lay it down. Let the peace be real

effects.log: You take the brush they offer you, and you sign, and you find your hand is quite steady.

choices.text: "Who said that I was asking?"

effects.log: They look up from the ledger, with mild interest, and they turn to a clean page. "I will let them know," they say.

events.text: The rain has stopped everywhere at once. In every temple you own, the incense has burned straight up and stayed there. There is someone waiting in your throne room, an old grey immortal with ink on one thumb: Ok-Seo, Recorder of the Jade Court. It seems that the Rolls were not made to hold a world with only one name. They are not angry. They only need to know how you would like it to end.

choices.text: Ask what happens to the people, and then sign

effects.log: They tell you. It is more than you hoped. You sign. Outside it begins to rain again, quite softly.

choices.text: Close the Rolls with your own hand

effects.log: They watch you do it. Nobody has ever done this. They seem a little sorry, and somewhat curious.

events.text: You have ruled all of it for a year, and in that year not one child under the sky has died in a war. This spring the sun has stopped, just under the hills, and in that red light a grey immortal named Ok-Seo walks up your road with the Jade Court's ledger. It is unfortunate, they say. It really is very good work. But the world below answers to the Court. Will you step aside, or must it be said louder?

choices.text: Step aside. It was for the children anyway

effects.log: You put down the seal, and the sun comes up. They nod, and write something down. You never learn what it was.

effects.log: They close the book, and the light goes on being red. It is going to be a long year.

events.text: There is a chair by the window, and a needle in your hand, and the sky has a long tear in it just over the Salt Pasture. You could sit down. Whoever sits here keeps the sky over the world below, for as long as they like. That is how it works, and that is what she did. You can see every lamp from here. You look at the chair for a good long while, and you can see why she stayed.

choices.text: Leave the chair empty. Let the sky be nobody's

effects.log: You put the needle down on the sill. Then you go to the door. It is a long way down, and for the first time in the history of the world there is no one up there at all.

choices.text: Mend the tear, then leave the chair empty

effects.log: You are bad at it. It is a crooked seam, and it can be seen on clear nights over the steppe. You put the needle down, and you go down the stair, and nobody is ever going to be up there again.

events.text: So this is how it goes. You had always thought there would be more noise. It is getting dark, in the wrong direction, and there is no pain in it to speak of. A very long way off, every bell in five empires has begun to ring without anybody having told them to. The people you conquered have come out of doors to look up. Some of them hated you. It seems, at the end, that they are standing there all the same.

choices.text: Look at them. Let them look at you

effects.log: You keep your eyes open as long as you can. It is the largest crowd that anyone has ever died in front of.

choices.text: Say it, one last time: "No."

effects.log: It does not carry very far. But it is written down, by an old grey clerk, in a very good hand, on a page that was supposed to be blank.

events.text: The sky has been quite polite about it. You are on your back, on the ground, and every one of your generals who is still alive has reached you by now, and nobody can think of anything to say. A very old cook has started to sing that terrible song. There is a lot of the world up there, and it is all still in the same place. You had thought you might move it. You did, a bit. They will find out later how much.

choices.text: Tell them to sing the second verse

effects.log: They sing it. It is ruder than the first. You get to about the middle of it.

choices.text: Ask who has the rearguard

effects.log: One of them tells you. It is quite the right answer. You nod, as if you had a war to run, and you stop.

events.text: You hear it break before you feel it, whatever it was. It is very far from the first thing you have broken. You are in a field, you notice, with a very good view, and someone has left a plum tree there. You had the whole world in your hand. You did get all of it. You went and asked the sky the only question that was worth asking, to its face, and it took three of them to answer. It is a nice evening.

choices.text: Laugh

effects.log: It hurts, and you do it anyway. It is heard, they say, in nine provinces, and in one small room at the top of a stair.

choices.text: Think about the plum tree at home

effects.log: It will be flowering about now. You had meant to go and see it. You had really been meaning to, one of these years.

events.text: You have laid it down. It takes about a month to tell everyone. The empires are given back their old names, and the old names are all quite pleased with themselves, and not one of them raises an army, because the sky has said that nobody may for a very long time. You find a house with a good roof. In the spring there is a child at the gate who has no idea who you are, and asks you if you know how to mend a kite.

choices.text: Mend the kite

effects.log: You are bad at it, and you get better. It is a good many years. Nobody under the sky goes to war in any of them, and when your time comes, you are sitting down.

choices.text: Show them how to mend it themselves

effects.log: It takes all afternoon. They fly it off over the wall, without thanking you. That goes on for a good many years, and you never do have to give another order.

events.text: The seals have all gone back. You kept one small thing, an inkstone that had been on your desk for all of the war. {auh_home} has written to ask you whether you would like a palace, and you did not answer. What you have done now cannot be undone, you are told, and there will be no war for three hundred years. You are very old, you find, or at any rate you are very tired. It is a nice day.

choices.text: Write the letters you never wrote

effects.log: There are a great many, and you do them all. Nobody can read your hand now. You do the last one in the afternoon, and you put the brush down, and you do not pick it up.

choices.text: Go and sit on the wall

effects.log: It is the Great Wall. There is nothing on the other side of it to be afraid of. There are sheep there. You watch them for a very long time.

events.text: You hold the seal for {auh_boy}, who is on the throne and is learning to read. A Regent minds a house. A Regent does not march on four empires in a child's name. The whole council tells you so, at length, and {auh_boy} sits above you on the nine steps with feet that do not reach the floor. When they have finished the boy asks, in a small clear voice, whether the map is big enough to get lost in.

choices.text: "Yes, Majesty. That is why I am going."

effects.log: He thinks about it. Then he nods, as he has been taught, and the edict goes out over his name. You wrote it. He will read it himself, one of these years.

choices.text: Answer the council, and leave the boy out of it

effects.log: You win the vote. The boy goes back to his lessons. Nobody has asked him anything else, and he has begun to notice who does not.

events.text: Every edict of this war will say the child commands it, and every province you take will be his. That is the law. The old tutor has come to point out what else it means: a Regent who wins all of this has made a boy the master of the world, and a boy grows up. Or the Regent has made something else of it. {auh_boy} has been told none of this. The tutor would like to know which of the two he should be teaching.

choices.text: "Teach him the map."

effects.log: The tutor bows, slowly. In the schoolroom there is now a large map with small flags, which the boy moves when the dispatches come. He is rarely wrong about where.

choices.text: "Teach him poetry."

effects.log: The tutor looks at you for some time. There is a great deal of poetry that winter. The boy is good at it, and he has started writing about regents.

events.text: The dispatch that reaches you at the front carries the child's first seal, in his own hand, a little crooked. {auh_boy} has pardoned a clerk. It is a small matter and an entirely wrong one, and half the council has already sent to tell you that it is not valid while you hold the seal. The other half has sent to tell you that it is. Somebody has been teaching him how a pardon is written.

choices.text: Let the pardon stand, and write him a note about it

effects.log: You tell him why the clerk was guilty. He writes back that he knows. It is the first letter you have ever had from him.

choices.text: Void it. There is one seal

effects.log: It is voided, by a rider, in front of the court. {auh_boy} says nothing at all. He is getting very good at that.

events.text: The Dowager's family have moved into the eastern palace to look after {auh_boy}, and they have brought a great many cousins, each of whom holds some small post with a very long title. Nobody has done anything that you could object to. Your own people at court have started to be sent on errands to the far provinces. The war is costing you the throne room, one desk at a time.

choices.text: Send the Dowager's brother a command at the front

effects.log: It is a great honour, and a long way off. He cannot refuse. The cousins are a good deal quieter without him.

choices.text: You will settle it when you come home

effects.log: You mean to. There are more cousins by the spring, and they have started to call the boy "Son of Heaven" in a way they did not used to.

events.text: All four empires have laid their seals at the feet of {auh_boy}, because the law says so, and you stood beside the throne and read out the words. He is the master of the whole world, and he has a cold. Afterwards he asks you, quite politely, when he might be allowed to sign something. Every governor in the hall has turned very slightly, to hear what you say. It has gone very quiet outside, and the wind has stopped.

choices.text: "Today, Majesty. Whatever you like."

effects.log: He signs for a kite. You watch him do it. Above the palace the sky has taken on a look of attention, and it is not looking at him.

choices.text: "When you are older."

effects.log: He nods. He has heard it before. Above the palace the sky has taken on a look of attention, and it is not looking at him.

events.text: It is done, in the name of a child, and there is not a soul under the sky who believes it was done by a child. The old tutor has told him all of it now. {auh_boy} comes to find you, by himself, at night, on the walls, which is forbidden. He wants to see it. So you stand there together. There is rather a lot of it. "They will come for you," he says. "Not for me." You had not told him that. You look up.

choices.text: "Who told you?"

effects.log: "Nobody," he says. "Look at it." He is quite right. There is something in the stars like a very long ruled line.

choices.text: Put your coat on him, and say nothing

effects.log: He lets you. It is much too big. You stay until the watch changes, and neither of you says anything else.

events.text: {auh_boy} is not a boy. You had a report about it, in among the rest, and did not read it, and now he has ridden to your headquarters with forty young men and very good manners. He kneels, as the law asks. Then he holds out his hand, palm up, as the law also asks, and waits for the seal of the regency. Every officer in the tent has found something to look at. You have held it for a long time.

choices.text: Give it to him, and ask for a General's warrant

effects.log: You put it in his hand. It is lighter than you remember. He signs your warrant on the spot, on a drum. You go on with the war, and you are a servant of the throne now.

choices.text: "Not while the war is on, Majesty."

effects.log: His hand stays out a moment longer. Then he thanks you, and rides home. The forty young men all look back at you as they go.

choices.text: Close his hand, and tell him there will be one throne

effects.log: He looks up. He has been expecting this since he was nine, and he does not look surprised. Your officers come forward, and nobody draws anything yet.

events.text: The Censors have read out the law in open court, and they have done it on the Emperor's birthday. A Regent holds the seal until the Son of Heaven comes of age. {auh_boy} has come of age. They have sent the reading to you at the front with four hundred signatures. The first of them is in a hand you know, a little crooked, grown a good deal steadier. There is also a short note. "You taught me to read," it says.

choices.text: Send back the seal, with a request for a warrant

effects.log: It goes by your fastest rider. The warrant comes back in nine days, and it is generous. He has not forgotten the note.

choices.text: Answer that the war must come first

effects.log: You write it very well. It is read out too. In the capital they have stopped lowering their voices.

choices.text: Answer that the Mandate goes where it is earned

effects.log: You write one line. It is the most dangerous line that anyone has written in three hundred years, and it is sent in your own hand.

events.text: You have come home for one month, and the Emperor receives you in the small garden, with no one by. {auh_boy} is taller than you. He pours the tea himself. He says he has read every dispatch of the war, and he thinks you were wrong about the Reef Castles, and he says why, and he is right. Then he sets down the pot and asks what you intend. He says it very gently. He has learned that from you as well.

choices.text: Take the seal off your belt, and put it by the pot

effects.log: He does not look at it for a while. "I will need a General," he says. "A good one." You drink the tea. It is not bad.

choices.text: "To finish it. Then we will talk."

effects.log: "Of course," he says, and pours you a little more. There are guards in that garden you did not notice when you came in.

choices.text: "To take the throne. You may have a very comfortable temple."

effects.log: He smiles, for the first time in years. "I wondered if you would say it to my face," he says. "Thank you."

events.text: {auh_gen} was sent to you from {auh_emp} to seal a peace, and has been in your house for a good many years. {ag_He} has heard the drums like everyone else. {ag_He} has come to your room, which {ag_he} does not often do, and sits down, and asks you nothing. On the table between you there is a map, and you did not think to turn it over. {ag_His} own city is on it, about a thumb's width from your hand.

choices.text: Tell {ag_him} everything you mean to do there

effects.log: You tell {ag_him}. {ag_He} listens to the end. "My brother will not kneel," {ag_he} says, and then {ag_he} tells you which gate.

choices.text: Turn the map over

effects.log: You turn it over. {ag_He} looks at the back of it for a while, and then {ag_he} gets up, and thanks you for your time.

events.text: You are told that {auh_gen} has stopped eating at your table. {ag_He} has taken to wearing the clothes {ag_he} came in, the ones from {auh_emp}, which do not fit so well now. Nobody in the house has said one word about it. The servants have started to take a long way round {ag_his} door. Your chief of guards has come to ask you, as a matter of routine, whether anyone should be reading {ag_his} letters.

choices.text: No. And tell {ag_him} you said no

effects.log: The guard goes away looking unhappy. {auh_gen} comes back to the table the next evening, in the old clothes, and says nothing, and eats.

choices.text: Yes. Every one

effects.log: They are very dull letters. They are about {ag_his} mother's knees. {ag_He} has known about your reader since the first day, and writes them for him.

events.text: You have {auh_emp} under your hand now. Its capital has your banner on it. {auh_gen} came to you from there to seal a peace, you remember, and that peace is what you have just walked through. {ag_He} is standing in the courtyard with one small box, packed. {ag_He} is not going anywhere, {ag_he} explains. There is nowhere that is still there. {ag_He} only wanted to see what it felt like to have it ready.

choices.text: Send {ag_him} home to rule it, in your name

effects.log: {ag_He} looks at you for a long time. "They will spit at me," {ag_he} says, and {ag_he} goes. The province is a great deal quieter with one of its own in the old rooms.

choices.text: Unpack the box with {ag_him}

effects.log: There is not much in it. It takes all afternoon. You do not talk about the war, and you never do again.

choices.text: Tell {ag_him} the matter is closed

effects.log: It is. {ag_He} bows, and picks up the box, and takes it back inside. It stays packed for the rest of {ag_his} life.

events.text: A delegation from {auh_emp} has come to your gate, and they have not asked for you. They have asked for {auh_gen}. They are the last of the old court, and they have brought {ag_him} the mourning white for {ag_his} family, on a tray, with their compliments. They would be interested to see {ag_him} put it on, here, in your house. It seems that they would be still more interested to see {ag_him} refuse.

choices.text: Stand beside {ag_him} while {ag_he} puts it on

effects.log: You stand there, in front of all of them. Nobody bows. They go home having seen something they did not come for, and they tell the province.

choices.text: Leave it to {ag_him}

effects.log: {ag_He} takes the tray, and thanks them, and shuts the door. You do not ask. {ag_He} is wearing grey when you next see {ag_him}.

choices.text: Have them put out on the road

effects.log: They are put out, quite gently. {auh_gen} watches from a window. You find you would rather not know how long.

events.text: A small neat person has asked to see you, and has brought a small neat list. This is {auh_spy}, who ran the eyes and ears of {auh_emp} until last month, and would like a position. The list is of everyone in your service who has ever taken its silver. You know eleven of the names, and you had dinner with one of them yesterday. They would like you to know that they are all very good at their work.

choices.text: Hire {auh_spy}, and keep every name where it is

effects.log: Those eleven go on sending their reports, and now you write them. It is a long time before the province knows who it is really talking to.

choices.text: Hang all of them, and {auh_spy} first

effects.log: It takes a week. Your service is a great deal cleaner and very frightened. Nobody brings you lists now.

choices.text: Burn the list, and send {auh_spy} home

effects.log: {auh_spy} watches it go, with interest. "I have a copy," they say. "Of course," you say. They seem pleased that you knew.

events.text: The court of {auh_emp} is gone, and nobody has told the people still working for it. One of them was found this month at your own quartermaster's desk, a pleasant grandmother who has been sending your grain figures for twenty-six years to a post box that no longer exists. She has been brought to you. She would like to know where to send them now. {auh_spy}, her old chief, has stopped answering.

choices.text: "To me, then. Same rates."

effects.log: She thinks it over, and asks about the arrears. You are now paying twenty-six years of someone else's wages, and your grain figures have never been so accurate.

choices.text: Make an example of her

effects.log: It is done in the square, by the book. Your quartermasters all go very quiet, and they are not any more honest than they were.

choices.text: Send her home with a pension

effects.log: She is rather offended. She had thought she was doing well. She sends you a note about your figures, which are wrong.

events.text: You wore the seal of {auh_emp} once, and you sat at that court. You knew all of them. Now its last spymaster, {auh_spy}, has been brought to you in a plain cart, and {auh_spy} has kept every report anyone ever wrote about you, in a neat bundle, tied with a green string. It seems that they had you down as promising. They have brought it along to give to you, or to anyone else who might care to read it.

choices.text: Read it, and hire them

effects.log: It is all there, and all correct, and there is a very good page on your faults. You keep it. They keep the green string.

choices.text: Burn it, and them with it, so to speak

effects.log: You have it done. You are the only one left who knows what that court thought of you. It is not as comfortable as you had expected.

choices.text: Give it back. You were who you were

effects.log: They look at you for rather a long time. "I wrote that you might do this," they say, and they find the page.

events.text: A grey immortal waits at the first gate of the Jade Court, one arm in a sling that has been there for some lifetimes. You know the ink on that thumb. "You will not remember breaking my brush," says Ok-Seo. "It was another life. I have the page." They hold it up. Nobody has been appointed to keep the clouds over the world below since. It has been noticed, here, at some length.

choices.text: Bow, and say nothing about the brush

effects.log: They return the bow, to exactly the depth the Rolls require. You are entered as a visitor. The whole of the Ministry has come out to look.

choices.text: Say you would do it again

effects.log: "Yes," says Ok-Seo. "It is written that you would." Half the Court will not sit in a room with you. The other half send, privately, to ask how it was done.

events.text: There is a small camp stool in the courtyard of the Ninth Host, kept very clean, that nobody is allowed to sit on. Star Marshal Cheolgang has come out to see you, walking a little carefully on one side. He looks you up and down. He cannot possibly know you, in this body, and he does. "Oh," he says, very much as he said it once before. Then he has the stool brought out and offers it to you, in front of his whole Host.

choices.text: Sit

effects.log: You sit. The Host looks straight ahead, nine thousand of them. There are a good many doors here that will now open, and rather more that will not.

choices.text: Decline, and stand with him

effects.log: You stand. He nods. It is the correct answer, he says, and he has been waiting a while to give someone the chance to get it right.

events.text: A clerk of the Jade Court brings you a single sheet, with apologies. It is the last page of a Mandate Roll, in a very good hand, and it has one word on it, in a place that was supposed to stay blank. You do not remember writing that. You are told you said it, on your back, in a field. Recorder Ok-Seo thought that you might like to have a copy.

choices.text: Keep it

effects.log: You put it away with what little you own up here. You look at it on bad days. It is a very short word.

choices.text: Send it back with your thanks

effects.log: It comes back again the next morning, without a note. Apparently that is not how the Rolls work.

events.text: Someone in the Ninth Host has been told who you were. A very large immortal in plain armour comes across the yard, and looks at you for some time, and then says that you were better than he had heard. He had the banners lowered for an hour, he says. Then he asks whether you have thought about the second form, because you dropped your left side, that time, and you are still doing it.

choices.text: Ask him to show you

effects.log: He shows you. It takes a season, and it is the most painful thing that has happened to you up here. Your left side stops dropping.

choices.text: Tell him that was another life

effects.log: "Yes," he says. "And the same left side." He goes away again, not at all offended.

events.text: The Mandate Rolls have an entry in your name, and it is the only one of its kind: a ruler of all the world below who took the brush when it was held out, and signed. The clerks of the Jade Court have been showing it to new arrivals as a model of correct procedure. You did not know this until a junior one recognised your soul and asked you, blushing, whether you would mind checking the form of his signature.

choices.text: Check his signature

effects.log: You check it. It is a little too proud in the last stroke. He is delighted. You will not lack for friends in the Ministries.

choices.text: Ask how the three hundred years turned out

effects.log: He looks it up. They held. There was a bad harvest in the two hundred and sixth, and nobody went to war over it. You go and sit on a cloud for a while.

events.text: An old woman is mending something at a window, on the far side of the clouds, and you have no reason to stop. But you do stop, and she looks up. "Sensible," she says, as if continuing a conversation. "I was not." She bites off the thread. She keeps a list of those who were offered her chair. It is not long. She has put a small mark beside you. You do not ask her what it means.

choices.text: Ask her anyway

effects.log: "It means that I am still here," says Seohwa. "Do come again." It is said at Court that nobody has ever been asked that before.

choices.text: Bow, and walk on

effects.log: You walk on. You can feel her go back to the seam. The clouds below you are a very little better mended than they were.

events.text: A file has reached the Heavenly Court, from the Recorder of the world below. It concerns you. An empire fell to you there, in an earlier life, or in this one, and such things are noted. It is not an accusation. A junior officer has been told to ask, with all courtesy, what you were trying to do, because nobody has been able to work it out from the file, and there is a box on the form.

choices.text: "Finish it."

effects.log: He writes it down. He looks at it, and looks at you, and he adds a small note. You will find, over the years, that your name gets to a desk before you do.

choices.text: "I was young."

effects.log: He writes that down too, with some relief. It is the usual answer, and there is a form for it.

events.text: There is a Star Sea seer at the gate who wishes to sell you something, as they do. It is a list of all those from the world below who ever took a whole empire and then came up here. It is a short list, and most of them are not doing very well. One keeps goats on a small cloud. One has not spoken in a thousand years. The seer would like to know whether you want to see how it ended.

choices.text: Pay, and read it

effects.log: You read it. It is good value. You do not sleep much that month, and you do not make their mistakes.

choices.text: Walk past

effects.log: You walk past. The seer shrugs, and makes a note of that as well, and sells it to someone else by evening.

events.text: The Moving City has stopped at last, and {auh_foe} rides out from it alone and draws a line in the grass with a lance. On the steppe a capital is a person. If you cross the line and fall, your host goes home, and they will let it. If they fall, there is nobody left that any clan would follow. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Cross the line

ok.log: {auh_foe} goes down at the last, in the long grass, without a sound. The whole of the Sworn Hundred gets off its horses.

fail.log: You wake up on a cart. They have been careful with you. They say you may come back, when you can sit a horse.

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You look at the line for a long time. Then you turn your horse. Nobody on the steppe will laugh. They will only remember.

events.text: The last camp of the Khaganate is a ring of ten thousand riders, and in the middle of it {auh_foe} is sitting on a saddle, eating. They wave you in with the bone. Your guards are told they may watch from the ring, if they keep their hands where they can be seen. It is the only way into the Moving City, and the Khagan has been told it will be quick. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Walk into the ring

ok.log: It is not quick. At the end of it {auh_foe} is on the ground, laughing, and ten thousand riders have gone very quiet.

fail.log: They stop it before it is finished. Somebody puts the bone in your hand. It seems to be a compliment. Your host goes home.

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You thank them for the invitation, and you take your army away in good order. {auh_foe} goes on eating.

events.text: All nine water gates of the Golden Barge City are shut, and {auh_foe} has had a platform built on the great canal, with a canopy over half of it and a very good view from every roof. By old custom the city may be surrendered only by its Admiral, and the Admiral may be persuaded in only one way. A small boat is waiting for you. It has a cushion. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Get in the boat

ok.log: {auh_foe} steps back off the edge of the platform, quite deliberately, and comes up laughing. All nine gates begin to open.

fail.log: You go into the canal. They fish you out with some ceremony. You are told there is no hurry: the city has outlived better.

choices.text: Send terms instead: the temples, the water law, and their name kept

ok.log: It takes nine days and a great many dinners. The gates open with music, and nobody in that city thinks they have lost.

fail.log: Your terms come back beautifully copied, with one word altered. It changes everything. You go home to think.

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You decline the cushion. It rains on your way out, and the whole city watches you go from under its awnings.

events.text: You are told that {auh_foe} has not lost on water in forty years, and you can believe it, having lost to them twice. The barges are lashed gunwale to gunwale across the mouth of the delta, and they have left one narrow plank road through the middle, wide enough for two people to meet. The priests have started the slow drums. Nobody will shoot, they promise. It would be very rude. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Walk the plank road

ok.log: You meet in the middle, and only one of you walks on. The drums stop. Somebody on the barges starts, very quietly, to unlash the ropes.

fail.log: You are carried back along the plank road by four polite young men. The drums keep time for you. Your campaign is over for now.

choices.text: Send an old abbot across instead, with an offer

ok.log: He is gone for a week. He comes back with the Admiral's seal in a basket of rice, and a list of what you have now promised.

fail.log: He comes back fatter, with a recipe. They were very pleased to see him. The barges stay where they are.

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You look at the plank road, and then you give the order to fall back upriver. It is not a thing you will be allowed to forget.

events.text: The Warden of the Morning Gate does not wait to be besieged. {auh_foe} has sent you a sword, the twin of their own, and a note: the keep has never been taken, and it will not be, but it could be given, once, to whoever is left standing on the sea stair at low tide. You have until the tide turns. Every lord in the Isles has rowed out to watch, and they have all brought lunch. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Go down to the sea stair

ok.log: {auh_foe} sets their blade down on the wet stone with both hands. Out on the water, one after another, the lords stand up in their boats.

fail.log: The tide comes in around your knees. They carry you up. The sword is sent after you, cleaned, with a note that says "Again, when you can."

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You send the sword back, with thanks. It is the correct thing to do, and everyone in the Isles knows exactly what it means.

events.text: {auh_foe} has laid out the challenge with perfect correctness. There is a square of raked sand in front of the Morning Gate, and two mats, and a very old man to call the exchanges, who has done this for eleven sea lords. Nothing can be done to the keep while a challenge stands. Nothing can be done about the challenge except to answer it. Your officers are all studying the sky. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Step onto the sand

ok.log: The old man calls the last exchange, and bows, for the first time in his life, to someone from the mainland. The keys are on your mat by evening.

fail.log: The old man calls it, kindly. You are helped off the sand. Your name is entered in the book, on a page with some very good company.

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You have a tent brought, and then you strike it. The old man rakes the sand again. It will keep.

events.text: There are a thousand steps to the White Palace, and {auh_foe} is standing on the five hundredth, with the White Guard ranged above and your host below. They have sent down word that nobody else need be hurt on these steps, which are holy. There is a good deal of air up here for someone who was born here. There is not nearly so much for you. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Climb to the five hundredth step

ok.log: At the end you are both sitting down, and {auh_foe} is unable to get up. Above you, slowly, the White Guard grounds its spears.

fail.log: You come down the steps a good deal faster than you went up. The monks bind you up without comment. There is no shame in the thin air, they say.

choices.text: Send up an offer: the scripture houses, the relic road, the old law

ok.log: The answer takes a month, and comes on the back of a very slow yak. It is yes. It has a great many conditions, and you will keep them.

fail.log: They send your offer down again with a correction in the third line, and their regrets. The steps are still there.

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You bow to the steps, and you take your army down to where there is air. It is a long way, and nobody stops you.

events.text: Dawn at the head of the last pass, and {auh_foe} has come out with a single lamp to meet you on the ice bridge. It is the only road to the Palace. It takes one person at a time, and has been holding up the Plateau's enemies for twelve hundred years, mostly by being narrow. They set the lamp down carefully, and they bow. Behind you, your army is trying very hard not to look at the drop. {auh_cap_word}

choices.text: Go out onto the bridge

ok.log: The lamp is still burning when it is over. You pick it up. You carry it across, and nobody on the far side lifts a hand.

fail.log: They could have let you go over the edge. They walk you back along the ice themselves, one step at a time, and set you down. You will be back.

choices.text: Set a lamp of your own on the ice, and send your terms across

ok.log: Theirs is lifted, and carried to yours, and the two are left there burning. It is the first treaty ever made on that bridge.

fail.log: Yours has gone out by the morning. Nobody touched it. You read the wind, and you go home.

choices.text: Pull the host back, and come again when you are stronger

effects.log: You bow across the ice, and leave them their bridge for another year. They leave the lamp out for you.

events.text: The physicians say you will ride in a season, and walk straight in two. The clans have sent you a very good mare for the journey, as they would for anyone who had crossed that line. {auh_foe} has sent word by the same rider: the grass will be there. Your officers are waiting to hear what the army is to be told. It has a right to know.

choices.text: Tell them you lost

effects.log: You tell them from a litter. They seem to think better of you. There are not many generals who have been that close to it and can say so.

choices.text: Tell them you were betrayed by the weather

effects.log: Nobody believes it. They are very kind about it. It goes into a song, and it does not rhyme with weather.

events.text: You are recovering at a temple on the Delta, as the guest of the people you have been trying to conquer. The rice is very good. Every morning a small boat comes by with {auh_foe}'s compliments and something for the wound, and it works. Your physicians have asked you to stop taking it. It has been explained to you that nobody has ever defeated this country. They have just been outlived.

choices.text: Keep taking it

effects.log: You mend very quickly. You find that you have put on weight, and that you have begun to know the names of the boats.

choices.text: Send it back, and leave at once

effects.log: You go north in a bad litter, and it takes a good deal longer. Nobody on the river is offended.

events.text: Your name is in the book at the Morning Gate, on the losing side, in a very fine hand. A copy has reached you. It says exactly what you did on the sand, stroke by stroke, and it is the most useful thing that you have ever read, and you would give a province not to have it in the world. Every young sword in the Isles can recite it by now. {auh_foe} has added a note in the margin: "Better than the last one."

choices.text: Learn it by heart

effects.log: You have it read to you while your arm mends. You begin to see it. There is a moment in the fourth exchange that you will not get wrong again.

choices.text: Have every copy you can find bought and burned

effects.log: It is an expensive winter. There are, it turns out, a great many copies.

events.text: They have brought you down to where you can breathe, and the air feels thick as soup. A very old monk sits with you while the ribs knit. He is not a physician. He has simply come to sit. After some days you ask him if {auh_foe} sent him, and he seems surprised, and says no: he goes to all of them. He has sat with four invaders, he says, and with one of those he is still in correspondence.

choices.text: Ask him how it ended for the other three

effects.log: He tells you, without any hurry. It takes the rest of the winter. You find it hard to say afterwards exactly what you have learned.

choices.text: Ask him when the passes open

effects.log: He tells you that, too. He has got the date exactly right. He does not seem to hold it against you.
